title: Enable CAR T cell immunotherapy in glioblastoma by modifying its microenvironment via oncolytic adenovirus encoding bispecific T cell engager
one_line: An oncolytic adenovirus (Ad5-\u039424-RGD) engineered to secrete an IL-13R\u03b12xCD3 BiTE was injected intratumorally and followed by systemic EGFR/EGFRvIII dual-targeted CAR T cells, producing superior tumor control in a subcutaneous U87 glioblastoma xenograft.
key_claims: OV-BiTE increased T cell recruitment to GBM in vitro and in vivo, with transwell assays showing significantly more T cells crossing the barrier than virus-alone or untreated controls.

In 3D GBM-BBB spheroids containing astrocytes, endothelial cells and pericytes, OV-BiTE downregulated the endothelial junction proteins Claudin-5, Occludin and ZO-1, increasing permeability and CAR T infiltration and cytotoxicity.

Intratumoral OV-BiTE followed three days later by intravenous combined EGFR + EGFRvIII CAR T cells reduced tumors more than OV-BiTE plus either CAR T alone, tracked by luminescence imaging over 31 days in tumors established for 20 days.
Explanted combination-group tumors showed reduced cellularity with necrotic/apoptotic debris, decreased IL-13R\u03b12-expressing cells, and deep human CD3+ T cell infiltration into the tumor core.

Combination treatment upregulated TNF-\u03b1, perforin and granzyme B in co-culture ELISpot assays; mice received a conservative single IV dose of 5\u00d710^6 CAR T cells with no body weight loss or overt toxicity signs.
limitations: All in vivo efficacy and safety data come from a subcutaneous flank xenograft, not an intracranial orthotopic model \u2014 a limitation the authors explicitly acknowledge.
A flank tumor has no physiological blood-brain barrier, glial network or CSF dynamics, so true BBB traversal was not tested in vivo.
Neuroinflammation and cerebral edema risk from deliberately downregulating Claudin-5/Occludin/ZO-1 in cerebral vasculature remains untested.
Xenograft model in immunodeficient mice cannot assess host antiviral clearance or endogenous immune contributions.
Manufacturing scalability of a custom viral vector plus autologous dual-targeted CAR T cells was not addressed experimentally.
open_questions: Does the OV-BiTE plus dual CAR T regimen control tumors in an intracranial orthotopic, immunocompetent GBM model without cerebral edema or neurotoxicity?
Is the tight-junction downregulation transient and reversible, and what is the magnitude of BBB opening in real cerebral vasculature?
Would allogeneic off-the-shelf dual-targeted CAR T cells retain the observed synergy and remove the manufacturing delay?
Does the multi-antigen crossfire actually prevent antigen escape on long-term follow-up or recurrence?
